title: Small-etale quasi-coherent modules and the presentation groupoid
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Locally Noetherian means that every etale scheme chart is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]; Noetherian means locally Noetherian, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, with quasi-separated meaning that the diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Modules on $X$ are on its small etale ringed site; quasi-coherence is [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. On a locally Noetherian space a module is coherent if it is quasi-coherent and its pullbacks to etale scheme charts are coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $p:U\to X$ be a representable surjective etale scheme atlas and let $(U,R,s,t,c,e,i)$ be its relation groupoid, with $R=U\times_XU$ and $s=\operatorname{pr}_1,t=\operatorname{pr}_0$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]. A groupoid module is a quasi-coherent scheme module $M$ on $U$ [pqf-def-coherent] with an isomorphism $\alpha:t^*M\simeq s^*M$ [def-pc-module-pullback], identity along $e$ and satisfying $c^*\alpha=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\alpha\circ\operatorname{pr}_0^*\alpha$ on composable pairs. Morphisms commute with these isomorphisms. Restriction to $U$ followed by the scheme etale/Zariski quasi-coherent identification gives an equivalence $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)\simeq\operatorname{QCoh}(U,R,s,t,c)$, sending $F$ to $(p^*F,\alpha_F)$ with its canonical pullback datum. If $X$ is locally Noetherian, $F$ is coherent if and only if the underlying scheme module $p^*F$ is coherent.

source.place: Tag 03M3 (proposition-quasi-coherent); spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 07UB (lemma-coherent-Noetherian), equivalence of coherence with coherence on a surjective etale scheme atlas.

proof.text: Write $F_V$ for the restriction of $F$ to an etale scheme chart, as supplied by the cartesian-chart characterization. Use the scheme etale/Zariski equivalence to regard these as ordinary scheme modules, compatibly with scheme pullbacks. Put $M=F_U$. For $t,s:R\to U$ the chart transition maps give $c_t:t^*M\simeq F_R$ and $c_s:s^*M\simeq F_R$; define $\alpha_F=c_s^{-1}c_t$. On the diagonal both maps are the same, so $e^*\alpha_F=1$. On $U\times_XU\times_XU$, cancellation of the middle transition gives $\alpha_{12}\alpha_{01}=\alpha_{02}$, which is the stated composition law with $s=\operatorname{pr}_1$ and $t=\operatorname{pr}_0$. A module map commutes with the $c_f$, hence with $\alpha_F$. This constructs the asserted restriction functor $K$.

source.place: Tag 03M3 (proposition-quasi-coherent), first paragraph of proof; Tag 03LZ (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent-small-etale).

proof.text: Given $(M,\alpha)$ and any chart $v:V\to X$, put $E_V=U\times_XV$, $a_V:E_V\to U$ and $b_V:E_V\to V$. Base change of the atlas is a surjective etale morphism of schemes; thus $\{b_V\}$ is an etale cover of the scheme $V$ and therefore an fpqc covering. The module $a_V^*M$ is quasi-coherent. On $E_V\times_VE_V=R\times_XV$ give it the pullback of $\alpha$; the identity and triple-overlap laws are exactly those of $\alpha$. Effective fpqc descent gives a quasi-coherent scheme module $N_V$ and an isomorphism $\theta_V:b_V^*N_V\xrightarrow{\sim}a_V^*M$ identifying the canonical datum with this pulled-back datum. Retain this identification as part of the descent, not merely an abstract isomorphism of underlying modules.

source.place: Tag 03M3 (proposition-quasi-coherent), converse construction through Descent Tag 023T (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent).

proof.text: For $f:V_1\to V_2$ over $X$ let $d=1_U\times f:E_{V_1}\to E_{V_2}$. Pullback composition and the identities $a_{V_2}d=a_{V_1}$, $b_{V_2}d=fb_{V_1}$ identify $b_{V_1}^*f^*N_{V_2}$ with $d^*b_{V_2}^*N_{V_2}$. On this cover use the isomorphism $\theta_{V_1}^{-1}d^*\theta_{V_2}$ to $b_{V_1}^*N_{V_1}$. It commutes with descent data: conjugating by the two $\theta$'s reduces its overlap square to the same pullback of $\alpha$ along $R\times_XV_1\to R$. Full faithfulness of scheme fpqc descent gives a unique isomorphism $c_f:f^*N_{V_2}\simeq N_{V_1}$ (its inverse descends by the same square). For $f=1$ the covered map is $\theta_V^{-1}\theta_V=1$. For $g:V_0\to V_1$, the covered composite $c_g\,g^*c_f$ is $\theta_{V_0}^{-1}(1_U\times(fg))^*\theta_{V_2}$ after cancellation of the middle $\theta_{V_1}$. Faithfulness gives $c_{fg}=c_g\,g^*c_f$. These are the transition maps missing from the source's displayed formula.

source.place: Tag 03M3 (proposition-quasi-coherent), omitted verification of transition isomorphisms and composition; expanded using full faithfulness in Descent Tag 023T.

proof.text: Convert $(N_V,c_f)$ to small-etale scheme modules by the scheme comparison and assemble them into $A(M,\alpha)$ by the cartesian-chart characterization. If $h:(M,\alpha)\to(M',\alpha')$ is equivariant, the maps $a_V^*h$ commute with overlap data and therefore descend uniquely, using $\theta_V$ and $\theta'_V$, to maps $h_V:N_V\to N'_V$. The transition square for $h_V$ holds after $b_{V_1}^*$ because it is the pullback square for $h$; faithfulness of descent makes it hold on $V_1$. The chart characterization then gives a unique map on $X$. Identity and composition hold after every cover and hence before it, by the same faithfulness. Thus $A$ is a functor.

source.place: Tag 03M3 (proposition-quasi-coherent), construction of the inverse functor; Tag 03LZ; Descent Tag 023T.

proof.text: For $F$ on $X$, the chart transition maps identify $b_V^*F_V$ with $a_V^*F_U$ on $E_V$, respecting the overlap datum by their composition law. Full faithfulness of scheme descent gives $N_V\simeq F_V$; uniqueness makes these isomorphisms commute with every $c_f$ and every map $F\to F'$. The chart characterization assembles a natural isomorphism $AK\simeq1$. Conversely, at $V=U$ the cover is $s:R\to U$ and the datum on $t^*M$ is the descent of $M$ via the identification $s^*M\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}}t^*M$. On $U\times_XU\times_XU$ this identification respects the datum precisely because $\alpha_{12}\alpha_{01}=\alpha_{02}$. Descent therefore gives $N_U\simeq M$. To check equivariance, pull its square on $R$ back to $U\times_XR$; the construction of $c_s,c_t$ in Step 3 makes the two composites the two sides of that same cocycle equation. Faithfulness of descent on the scheme $R$ gives the square on $R$. Uniqueness also gives naturality in $M$. Hence $KA\simeq1$ as groupoid-module functors, proving the equivalence.

source.place: Tag 03M3 (proposition-quasi-coherent), omitted verification of the inverse identities, with full faithfulness of Descent Tag 023T.

proof.text: Assume now that $X$ is locally Noetherian. If $F$ is coherent, its pullback to $U$ is coherent by the stated chartwise definition. For the converse suppose $M=p^*F$ is coherent. It is of finite type by the locally Noetherian scheme criterion. Fix any etale scheme chart $V\to X$ and form $E_V$ as above; both $U$ and $V$ are locally Noetherian by the definition for $X$. Under the chart and scheme comparisons, $b_V^*F_V\simeq a_V^*M$. The right side is of finite type by preservation of finite type under scheme pullback. The left side is the pullback of the quasi-coherent module $F_V$. The cover $b_V$ is fpqc as in Step 2, so finite-type descent gives that $F_V$ is of finite type. The locally Noetherian scheme criterion then makes $F_V$ coherent. This holds for every chart $V$, exactly the definition of coherence on $X$. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, or Noetherian hypothesis on $X$ was used for the equivalence.

source.place: Tag 07UB (lemma-coherent-Noetherian), equivalence of chart criteria, via scheme Tag 01XZ, Modules Tag 01B6, and Descent Tag 05AZ.
